# CloudKit schema v2: generated summary

<!-- Generated by scripts/schema/generate.mjs from schema/cloudkit-schema.json. Do not edit: change the JSON and run `node scripts/schema/generate.mjs` (docs/cloudkit-schema-design.md §12.1). -->

Schema revision 1, envelope 1, container `iCloud.com.foreverlm.knowledge`. The design and the reasons are in [docs/cloudkit-schema-design.md](../../docs/cloudkit-schema-design.md); this page lists what the schema file says, field by field.

Every record type has the system fields and one app field, `payload` (ENCRYPTED BYTES): a JSON envelope (`env`, `type`, `id`, `rev`, `saltID`, `fields`, `stamps`) with a stamp per field. `Content` adds `data` (ENCRYPTED BYTES) and `asset` (ASSET). Every plain scalar string field spills into a `field.<name>` satellite above 32 KiB unless marked otherwise. Policies: **L** last writer: the larger stamp wins; **S** server first: field-level compare-and-set against the base the writer saw; **X** maximum by value; the result carries the larger stamp; **N** minimum by value; the result carries the larger stamp; **T** text body: an L pointer to a body satellite, plus a three-way text merge when both sides changed since the base.

## Zones

| Zone | Database | Fetched | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Library` | private | changes | Structure and all personal state. |
| `Catalog` | private | changes | Source and Collection metadata, and playlist Entries. |
| `Content` | private | byName | Immutable byte satellites of the private library and every personal satellite; never change-fetched. |
| `Space-<uuid>` | private|shared | lightWalk | One zone per team, family, shared notebook or shared Doc, with a zone-wide CKShare; holds its satellites inline. |

### ZoneRoot

One per zone that holds records: the zone's kind, salt, owner and coordination leases; on the personal root also the cutover's seed, the late-import base and watermark, and the move maps. (§3.5.1)

Home: `current` (the library it is written in; `Library` in the personal library).

| Field | JSON | Kind | Policy | Req | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string (ZoneKind) | scalar | S | ✓ | What the zone is. |
| `salt` | base64 | scalar | S | ✓ | Base64 of 32 random bytes: the HMAC key for record names in this zone (and in Catalog and Content for the personal root). |
| `saltID` | saltID | scalar | S | ✓ | First 8 hex characters of sha256 of the salt bytes; repeated in every payload of the zone (§2.4 step 6). |
| `name` | string | scalar | L |  | Space name; empty for personal. |
| `owner` | Person | scalar | S | spaces | The space owner. |
| `createdAt` | ms | scalar | S | ✓ |  |
| `minClientRevision` | int | scalar | X | ✓ | Clients whose schema revision is lower stop sending to this zone and ask for an update (§12.5); starts at 1. |
| `seed` | json | map | L | personal root | Cutover coordination (§13.4), one key per subfield: state (pending\|seeding\|complete, SeedState), startedAt, canaryPassedAt, metadataCompleteAt, completedAt, counts {records, satellites, bytes} and manifest (a FileRef). Each subfield merges on its own, so a save that writes one (the claim's state, Finish's completedAt and counts, a fold's manifest) never drops another. metadataCompleteAt (set with the canary) lets other Macs reconcile and the web, the hosted MCP and iPhone build N switch while satellites still upload; manifest is a gzip satellite listing every (type, id) the seed uploaded (§13.5). A Mac that holds no library writes state pending; for a brand-new account a Mac, the iPhone or the web that holds none writes an empty complete seed (counts 0, every time set); none of them ever writes seeding, and the hosted MCP writes no root (§2.4). Keys: state, startedAt, canaryPassedAt, metadataCompleteAt, completedAt, counts, manifest. |
| `manifestDeltas` | FileRef | map | L |  | Personal root only: one gzip list per pass that created records after the seed manifest was written (any Mac's import pass, refresh, deferred catch-up, takeover, P6, reconcile upload; §13.6): the (type, id) it created, or (spaceID, type, id) for a space record. Each pass writes only its own key, so concurrent passes never collide. Every reader takes the manifest and every delta as "was in the new world" (§13.5, §13.6). Past 32 entries the importer folds them and the manifest into a new seed.manifest satellite and clears the folded keys in the same save, so the root stays small. Keys: <deviceID>.<passID>: the device and the pass that created the records. |
| `seedClaim` | object | scalar | S |  | {device, leaseUntil}: who seeds; a 30-minute lease renewed every 10 minutes by the holder; an expired claim is taken over by a CAS save (§13.4 step 1); never claimed by a Mac that holds no library. |
| `maintenanceLease` | object | scalar | S |  | {device, leaseUntil}: who runs GC, the orphan janitor, duplicate resolution, moveMaps folding and the practices engine; a 24-hour lease renewed daily. Macs only, and only one that holds the library: the seeder takes it with its claim; any other Mac only after seed.metadataCompleteAt and its own first complete fetch of Library and Catalog. Once the seed is complete, its holder is also the importer (§13.6). |
| `legacyImport` | object | scalar | L | personal root | {container, zones, tokens: {<old zone>: base64 change token}, lastOldWriteAt, quietSince, finishedAt, removedAt}: the late-import watermark (§13.6); published with legacyBase in P0 (§13.4) and advanced only by the importer: the seed-claim holder until the seed completes, then the maintenance-lease holder. |
| `legacyBase` | FileRef | map | L |  | Personal root only: the shared late-import base (§13.6). Per old record: its change tag, whether it is waiting (a value it gives waits for a record not created yet, §13.6), and for each v2 record the §10 mapping gives it, whether it owns that record (§10, "Who owns what") and a hash of each field, keyed by v2 type, id and field; a body hashes by the content hash its FileRef carries, which for a Doc is the old bodyRevision (§13.6). 64 gzip shards, est. 2–4 MB in all, so every shard stores inline (≈ 30–60 KB each, ≤ 256 KiB; 64 inline shards hold up to 16 MB). Published by the seeder in P0, before its first record (§13.4); advanced only by the importer. Keys: shard: 00–3f, the first byte of sha256(old record name) divided by 4, as two hex characters. |
| `learnerModel` | FileRef | scalar | L |  | Personal root only: the learner-model satellite in private Content. Personal satellite. |
| `archiveIndex` | FileRef | map | L |  | Personal root only: a gzip list of (type, id) per archive zone, rewritten after each archive move batch (§11.4). Keys: archive zone name. |
| `moveMaps` | FileRef | map | L |  | Personal root only (D51): one entry per SpaceMoveJob pass (a notebook moved into a space, a Doc moved into its Doc space, a reverse move; a course never moves, §5.5), a gzip list of the (type, id, from zone, to zone) that pass moved. Each is written before the pass deletes its first original and is never rewritten, so two Macs' passes never lose each other's ids. Past 32 entries the maintenance Mac folds them into one folded.<n> entry and clears the folded keys in the same save (§4.4). Keys: <moveJobID>.<pass>, or folded.<n> for folded entries. |
| `familyPlanCode` | string | scalar | L |  | Family spaces (was the Team payload, schema 137). |
| `sealedMemberKeys` | base64 | map | L |  | Family member AI keys, each sealed to the member's device key. Keys: CloudKit user record name. |
| `assignmentsNotebookID` | id → Notebook | scalar | S |  | Family: the fixed Assignments notebook. |
| `primaryID` | id → Notebook \\| Artifact | scalar | S | kind ∈ {notebook, doc} | The notebook or Doc the space was made for. |
| `editedAt` | ms | scalar | X | ✓ | Ms of the last content change. |

### Source

A work in the library: its identity, metadata and pointers to its content satellites. 1.5–2.5 KB. Nothing member-local: how a source entered a member's library is that member's Mark(provenance). (§3.5.4)

Home: `current` (the library it is written in; `Catalog` in the personal library).

Id: URL sources src_ + hex(sha256("source:v1:" + URLNormalizer.normalize(url))) (SourceIdentity.stableID). A file captured on the iPhone or the web (a scan, photos, a PDF, a shared PDF) gets SourceIdentity.fileID(sha256) = src_ + hex(sha256("source:v1:file:" + <sha256 hex of the bytes>)), so the same bytes captured twice land on one id (D47); the Mac's own file imports keep their path-based ids and gain the file: work key. Every other kind keeps its documented rule (§4.1). The same id in every zone.

| Field | JSON | Kind | Policy | Req | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `workKeys` | workKey | set | L | ✓ | Every identity key known (includes primaryKey); looked up before any mint (§4.2). |
| `type` | string (SourceType) | scalar | L | ✓ | move_source_type edits it; a skeletal import writes it with a provisional stamp. |

| `language` | string | scalar | L |  |  |

| `status` | string (ArchiveStatus) | scalar | L | ✓ | Shared state: in a space it is the team's archive; a copy into a space starts active. |
| `ingest` | object | scalar | X | ✓ | {ord: [generation, rank], state: queued\|fetching\|ready\|error\|paywalled, error?, at, device}: monotonic by ord (rank queued 1, fetching 2, error 3, paywalled 3, ready 4; generation + 1 on a deliberate re-fetch); written by the ingesting device; a paper is ready only with a PDF; a skeletal import writes [0, 1], so it never sends a ready source back to queued. |

Keys: documented per type. |

### Notebook

A notebook. Notes live in its Notes Doc (Artifact notes:<id>); membership, ticks and order are not in this record. A merged or moved notebook stays for ever as a stub (status merged or moved); a late edit to one of its other fields is forwarded once, through the fold to a merge's survivor or verbatim to the space copy (§5.2). (§3.5.6)

Home: `current` (the library it is written in; `Library` in the personal library).

Id: Some existing ids are uppercase UUIDs; ids compare exactly.

Being listed feeds no context: each member ticks listed notebooks into their own chats' context in NotebookState.contextNotebooks, and the Studio never reads them (D52, §5.6). |

### Entry

The ordered edge: an item in a notebook, goal, lesson or playlist. The same item added to the same container on two devices gets the same record name. An Entry whose item is missing is kept and hidden on read; twin and merged Entries copy state and approval values and stamps verbatim (§5.6). (§3.5.8)

Zone: Catalog holds playlist Entries only; notebook, goal and lesson Entries are in Library or the container's space.

Home: `parent` (the zone of `containerID`: notebook → Notebook, goal → Goal, lesson → Lesson, playlist → Collection; by `containerKind`).

Id: A second span of the same source in one lesson takes #2, then #3; the first has no suffix.

| Field | JSON | Kind | Policy | Req | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `containerKind` | string (EntryContainerKind) | scalar | S | ✓ |  |
| `containerID` | id → Notebook \\| Goal \\| Lesson \\| Collection | scalar | S | ✓ | The back-pointer every merge, split and delete re-points. |
| `itemKind` | string (EntryItemKind) | scalar | S | ✓ |  |
| `itemID` | id → Source \\| Artifact \\| Course \\| Quiz | scalar | S | ✓ | A notebook's Entry of itemKind course is its follow of that course, the one tie between the two (§5.5). In the same library (the private library = Library + Catalog + Content; a space = its zone); the items of personal containers (Goal) resolve by wire id across the personal library and every space. |

### Sitting

One sitting of answers (cards, a quiz, a walk, a bout) by one device, the only writer of its answers; its L fields (endedAt, breakEndsAt) merge normally. Saved at most every 30 s while it runs, at its end and when the app goes to the background (D44). (§3.5.23)

Home: `library` (always the personal Library).

Id: Migrated attempts: sit:legacy: + the first 24 hex characters of sha256(session:<session_id>, or day:<YYYY-MM-DD>); each migrated quiz score (courseQuiz.score.*, lectureQuiz.score.*) is a Sitting of its own, sit:legacy: + 24 hex of sha256(quiz:<courseQuiz|lectureQuiz>:<preference key>). Migrated Sittings carry deviceID legacy22 and are written by the seeder and, for old-world attempts and scores that arrive after T0, by the late importer; both only add answers (§13.6). A new part <firstID>#2, #3… starts at 200 answers or 128 KiB.

### ActivityLog

One device's engagement on one day, written debounced every 5 minutes while active and at background; a device's own log holds only what generation-2 code records on it. Everything generation-1 code recorded, on any device, lives in the al:<day>:legacy22 logs, built by the seeder and extended by the late importer by maximum per (day, source) and per (day, old device), never by sum. The day's fold sums engagedSeconds, review.seconds and the reviewByDevice values over all logs and takes the maximum maxFraction. (§3.5.24)

Home: `library` (always the personal Library).

| Field | JSON | Kind | Policy | Req | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | day | scalar | S | ✓ |  |
| `deviceID` | deviceID | scalar | S | ✓ | The only writer (for legacy22, the seeder and the late importer, which merge per element). |

| `review` | object | scalar | L |  | {seconds, cardsAnswered}: the goal clock (was MemoryReviewActivity). |
| `reviewByDevice` | object | map | L |  | Legacy logs only: oldDeviceID → {activeSeconds, goalSeconds}, the old per-device rows of memory_review_activity; the fold sums them; late import keeps the maximum per (day, old device). Keys: old device id (memory_review_activity.device_id). |
| `editedAt` | ms | scalar | X | ✓ | Ms of the last content change. |

### Content

An immutable byte satellite named by owner, role and the hash of its stored bytes; fetched by name, never change-fetched. A create collision counts as success only after the stored part fields (partHash, partBytes, enc) match; hash, size, part and parts describe the file of whoever uploaded the part first (§3.5.30 rule 1). (§3.5.30)

Zone: Content for private owners and every personal satellite; the owner's space for space owners.

Home: `owner` (the zone of `ownerType` `ownerID`; `Content` for a private owner or a personal `role`).

Id: partHash32 = the first 32 hex characters of sha256 of that part's stored bytes (after gzip when enc = gzip); the FileRef lists every part's hash, so every name follows from it.

| Field | JSON | Kind | Policy | Req | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ownerType` | string | scalar | S | ✓ | The record type of the owner. Never spills. |
| `ownerID` | id | scalar | S | ✓ | The owner's logical id. |
| `role` | string | scalar | S | ✓ | A role from satelliteRoles. Never spills. |
| `hash` | sha256hex | scalar | S | ✓ | sha256 of the whole decoded file (all parts reassembled and decoded) as the part's first uploader had it; a later file that shares the part may differ, so a collision never compares it. |
| `size` | int | scalar | S | ✓ | Decoded bytes of the whole content. |
| `mime` | string | scalar | S | ✓ | Never spills. |
| `enc` | string (FileEncoding) | scalar | S | ✓ |  |
| `part` | int | scalar | S | ✓ | 0…parts−1. |
| `parts` | int | scalar | S | ✓ | ≥ 1; parts are exactly 48 MiB (native) or 14 MiB (web), the last smaller. |
| `partHash` | sha256hex | scalar | S | ✓ | sha256 of this part's stored bytes; its first 32 hex characters are in the name. |
| `partBytes` | int | scalar | S | ✓ | Stored bytes of this part. |
| `personal` | bool | scalar | S | ✓ | A personal satellite (understanding, learner model, draft base): always in private Content, never in a space. |
| `gen` | object | scalar | S |  | {model, prompt, input, device, at} for machine output. |
| `createdAt` | ms | scalar | S | ✓ |  |

## Shapes

| Shape | JSON | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Person` | {"user": "<CloudKit user record name>", "name": "<display name>"} | Container-scoped; used only in spaces. |
| `ItemRef` | "<kind>:<id>" with an optional "#<subKey>" | Examples: src:src_2cd9…#idea-17, qz:cq-1913…#q3, wk:doi:10.1038/x. |
| `Locator` | {"t": "pdf"\|"text"\|"epub"\|"media"\|"web"\|"slide"\|"doc", …} | pdf {page, quads: [[x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3,x4,y4]], offset?} with page-normalized 0…1 quads, origin top-left; text {offset, len, quote, prefix, suffix, textHash}; epub {href, cfi, fraction}; media {seconds, end?, duration}; web {fraction}; slide {index, seconds}; doc {bodyHash, start, end, quote}. Unknown kinds and keys are kept. |
| `Span` | {"from": Locator, "to": Locator} | Lesson item ranges: pages 12–40, 00:10–00:45, one EPUB chapter. |
| `ReaderContext` | {"spaceID"?, "notebookID"?, "courseID"?, "lessonID"?, "chatID"?} | Provenance of a write; never forks state. |
| `FileRef` | {"owner", "role", "hash", "size", "mime", "enc": "identity"\|"gzip", "stored", "parts": ["<partHash32>", …], "inline", "children": [FileRef], "gen"?: {model, prompt, input, device, at}, "heldBy"?: deviceID} | A pointer to Content satellites (§3.3). owner = the record that first uploaded the bytes (a copy of the FileRef keeps it, D41); hash = sha256 hex of the decoded bytes; size = decoded bytes; stored = stored bytes; parts = the first 32 hex characters of sha256 of each part's stored bytes, in order, so every satellite name ct:<owner>:<role>:<partHash32> follows from the FileRef; inline = one part held in data; children list dependent satellites so GC never parses bodies; heldBy = the bytes were not uploaded (sync.originals) and live only on that Mac. |
| `MadeBy` | {"route", "device", "at", "model"?, "chatID"?} | Provenance of a record. |
| `SettingValue` | {"t": "bool"\|"int"\|"double"\|"string"\|"array"\|"dict"\|"data"\|"date", "v": …} | Typed JSON (data = base64, date = ms); null = cleared. |
| `Answer` | {"subject": ItemRef, "at", "prompt"?, "response"?, "rating"?, "score"?, "correct"?, "outcome"?, "counted", "practice", "latencyMs"?, "variant"?, "gradeState"?, "feedback"?, "evidence"?, "model"?, "curriculumFingerprint"?} | One answer in a Sitting; written once. subject is crd:<id>, qz:<id>#<qid>, src:<id>#walk:<step> or exc:<id>; outcome is graded:<verdict>, remembered, forgot or skipped. Answers that do not count toward scheduling are written too (counted: false). |
| `SpilledString` | {"$file": FileRef} | A string field whose UTF-8 encoding passed spillStringBytes, uploaded as a field.<name> satellite (gzip) and resolved by every reader (§3.2 rule 8). |

## Settings

The Setting record keys (§3.5.3): one record per key, account scope in Library and space scope in a space. Generated into schema/generated/settings-catalog.json, which the hosted MCP and the web validate Setting writes against; ForeverLMMacUnitTests/SettingsCatalogTests fails when it and the app disagree (SyncedPreferenceKeys, set_app_setting's catalog, AITaskSettingsCatalog). keys and families list every synced key and prefix that stays a Setting; records lists the ones generation 2 moves into typed records (the domain prefixes of §10, which are not Settings), origin spec marking one the spec maps before every generation-1 build writes it; leftOut lists the synced prefixes that stay Settings but stay out of the catalog, because only their own writers set them, never set_app_setting. type is SettingValue.t; mcp names how a chat sets the key (derived: the setter computes it); retired keys are kept for older builds and never written; origin spec marks a key the spec defines that no client writes yet. The catalog is `schema/generated/settings-catalog.json`.

| Key | Type | Scope | MCP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account.displayName` | string | account | `set_app_setting` account.display_name | The name the account button, the account menu and the chat greeting show, on every Mac and the web. |
| `account.showsCompCrown` | bool | account | `set_app_setting` account.show_comp_crown | Whether an account whose AI usage ForeverLM pays for shows it: the Mac account menu's "Usage is paid for" row and the crown in the web's account footer (the Mac's account button carries no crown since 2026-10-06); true when absent. |
| `account.aboutYou` | string | account | `set_app_setting` account.about_you | Where the learner is coming from, in their words (LearnerProfile.aboutYouPreferenceKey); every course tailors to it. |
| `aiSpend.backgroundDailyCapUSD` | double | account | `set_app_setting` billing.background_daily_cap_usd | Background AI's daily limit in US dollars (BackgroundAIDailyCap); absent or 0 means off. 0 to 250. |
| `aiSpend.stoppedSteps` | array | account | `resume_ai_work` steps (derived) | The background steps the learner stopped under Running in the background or with cancel_ai_work (AIInFlightCalls.stoppedStepsKey; AI task ids, ledger task keys and automatic_audio, strings): none runs on any Mac until resumed. Absent means none. |
| `ai_provider` | string | account | `set_ai_task_settings` target default_model provider (derived) | The Default Model's provider, kept current for older builds beside aiRoute.defaultChat. |

Families (a pattern is literal text with `<name>` placeholders; `parts` restricts a placeholder, `aiTasks` meaning the AI task ids):

| Pattern | Type | Scope | MCP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aiTask.<task>.prompt` | string | account |  | Retired: a task's custom prompt, in place of the built-in one (KeychainService.taskPrompt). No control or tool sets one any more (setTaskPrompt has no caller); a value an older build wrote is still read. Retired. Parts: task ∈ aiTasks. |
| `aiTask.<task>.<field>` | string | account |  | Retired 2026-09-28: no task has a model of its own (KeychainService.purgeRetiredTaskModels drops them; the chat's picks are per session). Retired. Parts: task ∈ aiTasks; field ∈ provider, model, effort, speed. |
| `aiRoute.task.<task>` | data | account |  | Retired 2026-09-28 with the per-task models; the chat's is only read as a legacy route. Retired. Parts: task ∈ aiTasks. |
| `aiHost.<slot>|<model>` | string | account | `set_ai_task_settings` target host host (derived) | Which OpenRouter host serves one model in one slot: OpenRouterHostPreference as JSON text; model is the lowercased slug. Parts: slot ∈ chat, background.text, background.images. |
| `aiHost.task.<task>|<model>` | string | account |  | Retired 2026-09-28 with the per-task models. Retired. Parts: task ∈ aiTasks. |
| `aiBackups.<slot>` | string | account | `set_ai_task_settings` target backups backups (derived) | The models a slot falls back to, in order: a JSON array of {provider, model}, at most AIBackupModels.limit (10). Parts: slot ∈ chat, background.text, background.images. |
| `aiBackups.task.<task>` | string | account |  | Retired 2026-09-28 with the per-task models. Retired. Parts: task ∈ aiTasks. |
| `aiBackground.provider` | string | account | `set_ai_task_settings` target background_text provider (derived) | Background's text provider, kept current for older builds beside aiRoute.background. |
| `aiBackground.model.<provider>` | string | account | `set_ai_task_settings` target background_text model (derived) | Background's text model for that provider (its AIProvider raw value), kept current beside aiRoute.background. |
| `aiBackground.usageConsented` | bool | account | `set_app_setting` background_ai.usage_consented | The learner agreed to background AI usage in Getting Started. |
| `aiBackground.meetingsMayUseFree` | bool | account | `set_ai_task_settings` target meetings meetings_may_use_free | Meeting tasks may run on a free Background model (MeetingModels.mayUseFreeKey). |
| `aiBackground.model` | string | account |  | Retired: the unsuffixed Background model, replaced by aiBackground.model.<provider>. Retired. |
| `aiBackground.metaFreeTrial.<flag>` | bool | account |  | Retired with the direct Meta trial (KeychainService.purgeRetiredProviderData). Retired. Parts: flag ∈ active, exhausted. |
| `aiBackground.metaFreeTrial.<number>` | double | account |  | Retired with the direct Meta trial: its start (epoch seconds) and its limit in dollars. Retired. Parts: number ∈ startedAt, limitUSD. |
| `readAloud.voiceRating.<model>|<voice>` | string | account | `set_app_setting` read_aloud.voice_rating | The learner's thumbs on one model's voice (ArticleSpeechVoiceRating); absent is no rating. One of up, down. |
| `memory.reviewDepth.type.<sourceType>` | string | account | `set_review_depth` depth | How much of a memory review a kind of source gets by default (MemoryReviewDepth); sourceType is lowercased. One of quick, standard, deep. |
| `notebook.thinkFirst.<notebookID>` | string | account | `update_notebook` think_first | One notebook's Think first level, the learner's own (account scope, so a teammate's choice never changes it), over thinkFirst.level; absent means the library's level applies. A Setting rather than a NotebookState field, like notebook.naming., so no store schema changes. One of off, summariesAndStudio, alsoChat. |
| `follow.<collectionID>` | dict | space |  | A space's explicit refresh of a followed Collection: {autoImport, runnerDeviceID}, naming the one member's Mac that imports the feed (§3.5.5). The Mac writes it through SpaceFollows, not as a synced preference: the catalog's origin spec only says no preference key carries it. Defined by the spec; no synced preference key carries it yet. |

Settings the catalog leaves out (only their own writers set them, never `set_app_setting`):

| Pattern | Type | Scope | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `map.layout.<mapID>` | string | account | One of the learner's canvases (docs/knowledge-map-design.md, "Canvases in the Space"), as a JSON string {version, placements, regions, edges, removed, name, created, trash} (KnowledgeMapLayout): each placed card's spot, each region the learner drew and each arrow, every entry stamped with the time it was written and every removal kept as a tombstone, so two copies merge entry by entry; and the canvas itself, its name and Trash mark stamped the same way and the second it was made. One row per canvas, and every row is a canvas listed in the Space: mapID is library for the first canvas, else cnv- and a lowercase UUID. Written by the Canvas pane, the Space and MCP's canvas tools on the Mac, never set_app_setting: a lens a chat asks for changes nothing until the learner keeps it. |
| `notebook.naming.<notebookID>` | string | account | The name and card description ForeverLM last put on a notebook made without a name, as a JSON string {title, summary?, sources?, exchanges?} (NotebookNaming.Mark): ForeverLM may rename the notebook only while its title and summary are still these. Absent means ForeverLM leaves the name alone; every learner edit of the title or description removes it. Written by the notebook creators and the naming step (Mac, iPhone, MCP create_project without a title), never set_app_setting. |
| `studio.workspaceView.<viewID>` | array | account | One saved workspace view per row (StudioSavedWorkspaceView), so monitor arrangements never contend: the window arrangement the learner saved with Save Workspace View, as the window's own stored form. Written by the window that saves or deletes it, never set_app_setting: a chat has no window to arrange. |
| `notebook.questions.<notebookID>` | string | account | The questions a notebook's guide suggested for its sources, and which were asked, as a JSON string {sources, questions, asked} (NotebookSuggestedQuestions.Kept): sources is the fingerprint of the notebook's source ids the questions were suggested for; the guide offers the questions not asked yet in every new chat without a model call, and offers Suggest questions again only when the fingerprint changes. Per member, one row per notebook. Written by the Mac's notebook chat when an answer suggests questions or one is asked, never set_app_setting. |
| `notebookCollection.<collectionID>` | string | account | A Notebook Collection's name (a leading emoji is its icon), one Setting per collection, null once the collection is deleted. Written by the collection writers (the Notebooks home on each client, MCP update_notebook_collection on the Mac), never set_app_setting (§3.5.3). |
| `pageSpace.<spaceID>` | string | account | The name of one of the learner's spaces of pages (PageSpaces; ChatGPT's spaces, the Space sidebar's Spaces), a leading emoji its icon; spaceID is psp- and a lowercase UUID. One Setting per space, null once the space is deleted. The learner's own grouping, not a sync space (D4): written by the Space sidebar on the Mac and the web and by MCP update_space on the Mac, never set_app_setting. |
| `page.space.<artifactID>` | string | account | The one space of pages (pageSpace.<spaceID>) a page, linked Google Doc, site or reading is in, as its spaceID; absent when it is in none. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the Doc: an id whose pageSpace name is gone (deleted, or not arrived yet) is read past, and deleting a space removes the rows naming it that the deleting device holds. Written by Move to Space and New page in a space on the Mac and the web, and by MCP update_space on the Mac, never set_app_setting. |
| `page.pinned.<artifactID>` | string | account | When the learner pinned a page, a linked Google Doc or a site (PagePins; ChatGPT's Pin, the Space sidebar's Pinned section), as the whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent when it is not pinned, and the newest pin lists first. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the Doc: only the learner's own pages pin, never a team's. Written by Pin and Unpin on the Mac and the web, never set_app_setting. |
| `page.parent.<childArtifactID>` | string | account | The page a page is nested under (PageParents; ChatGPT's subpages, the Space lists' nested rows), as the parent's Artifact id; absent when the page is top-level. One Setting per child, per member, never a field of the Doc: only the learner's own Markdown pages nest, under another of their own, never a team's. An id that names a page that is gone, in Trash or not the learner's own is read past (its children list at the top and the row stays, so restoring the parent brings them back), and a cycle two devices made at once is cut at its smallest id. Written by Move to Page, New Subpage, Remove from Parent and the editor's Page row on the Mac, never set_app_setting. |
| `spaceList.<listID>` | string | account | One of the learner's lists in the Space (SpaceLists; ChatGPT's To-do list among the pages): a list of goals or of ideas, as a JSON string {kind: goals\|ideas, name, created, at, trashed} in seconds since 1970, trashed absent while it is in use; listID is lst- and a lowercase UUID. One Setting per list, the newer write winning whole, null once deleted forever. The learner's own grouping: the goals and ideas stay records of their own. Written by the Space on the Mac and by MCP's list tools there, never set_app_setting. |
| `spaceListItem.<recordID>` | string | account | The one list in the Space (spaceList.<listID>) a goal or an idea is in, as its listID; absent when it is in none. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the goal or idea: an id whose list row is gone is read past, and deleting a list removes the rows naming it that the deleting device holds. Written by the Space on the Mac and by MCP's list tools there, never set_app_setting. |
| `images.notebookCoverBackfill.<zoneID>` | dict | account | The cover backfill's claim and completion marker for one zone (D53, §5.9): {state: running\|done, by: deviceID, at}, in Library, a space's in its owner's Library. No synced preference: only the backfill on the maintenance Mac writes it, by a compare-and-set save beside the engine, never through user_preferences; set_app_setting on the Mac and in the hosted MCP refuses it, and the web and the iPhone never write it. |
